name: Equal regard for friend and foe
meaning: The steady person has the same regard for well-wishers, friends, enemies, neutral people, relatives and even the wicked.
applies_when: Someone is treating people very differently depending on whether they like them, or is caught in factional conflict.
misleads_when: It is used to deny the right to keep away from people who are harmful. Equal regard does not mean equal trust or access.
modern_application: Treat the person you are in conflict with exactly as courteously as you would a stranger, while keeping whatever boundary you need.

name: Bear no hatred; be friendly and compassionate
meaning: The devotee dear to God bears no hatred towards any being, is friendly and compassionate, free of possessiveness and ego, and forgiving.
applies_when: Resentment towards someone is consuming the person.
misleads_when: It is used to pressure a victim to drop justified anger or to stay in contact with an abuser.
modern_application: You can let go of hatred without excusing what happened. Write what you need for your own peace, separate from what the other person deserves.

name: Do not trouble others, and do not be troubled
meaning: Dear to God is one from whom the world does not shrink, and who does not shrink from the world.
applies_when: Someone is creating friction around them, or is constantly unsettled by others.
misleads_when: It is used to silence someone raising a legitimate concern.
modern_application: Before your next difficult conversation, decide how you will stay calm and how you will avoid making the other person defensive.

name: Feel others' joy and pain as your own
meaning: The highest yogi is the one who, comparing with oneself, sees the same pleasure and pain in all beings.
applies_when: Someone needs to understand another person's position in a conflict.
misleads_when: It leads to taking on others' distress to the point of burnout.
modern_application: Describe the situation from the other person's side in the first person ('I feel…'), then reread your own plan.

name: Speak truthfully, kindly and helpfully
meaning: The discipline of speech is speech that causes no distress and is true, pleasant and beneficial.
applies_when: Someone has to deliver hard news, give feedback, or is tempted to say something cruel.
misleads_when: It is used to avoid ever saying a necessary hard truth. Truth comes first in the list.
modern_application: Run what you plan to say through three filters: is it true, is it kind in how it is said, and does it help?

name: Forgiveness belongs to the strong
meaning: Forgiveness, fortitude and freedom from malice are listed among the divine qualities, alongside vigour.
applies_when: Someone is deciding whether to forgive a family member, friend or colleague.
misleads_when: It is used to demand immediate forgiveness from someone who was harmed, or to restore access to someone dangerous. Forgiving is not the same as reconciling.
modern_application: Decide separately: (1) do I want to release this resentment for my own peace? (2) do I want this person back in my life, and on what terms?

name: Own your words and ask forgiveness
meaning: After seeing who Krishna truly is, Arjuna asks forgiveness for every careless or disrespectful word, 'as a father bears with a son, a friend with a friend'.
applies_when: Someone realises they have taken a person for granted or spoken carelessly.
misleads_when: It is used to force an apology from someone who did nothing wrong.
modern_application: Name the specific words or acts, without excuses, and ask what would help make it right.

name: Seek peace with a parent's anger
meaning: Offered three boons by Death, Nachiketas's first wish is that his angry father be calm, cheerful and free of anger towards him, and welcome him home.
applies_when: A strained relationship with a parent, where one wants reconciliation.
misleads_when: It is used to tell a young person to appease a parent who is abusive or dangerous. Safety comes first, and leaving danger is always supported.
modern_application: Write what you would most wish for your relationship with your parent, not what you wish they would admit. Start from that.

name: Learn together without hostility
meaning: The Katha ends with a prayer for teacher and student: may we work together with vigour, may our study be bright, may we not hate each other.
applies_when: Friction between a student and teacher, mentor and mentee, or study partners.
misleads_when: It is used to excuse a teacher's mistreatment of a student.
modern_application: Begin your next session with the person by naming the shared goal you are both working towards.

name: Delight in the welfare of all beings
meaning: The sages who reach peace delight in the welfare of all beings; even those who follow the hardest inner path are marked by this.
applies_when: Envy or rivalry makes someone unable to be glad of others' good fortune.
misleads_when: It is used to deny one's own needs.
modern_application: When you hear of someone's success this week, send them a genuine word of congratulation.

name: Non-violence
meaning: Non-violence appears in every list of virtues: in knowledge, in the divine qualities, and among the states that come from God.
applies_when: Someone is tempted to hurt another, physically or verbally, or to retaliate.
misleads_when: It is used to tell someone they may not defend themselves or leave a violent situation.
modern_application: Before responding to provocation, ask: is there a way to protect what matters without causing harm?

name: Truth is the home of wisdom
meaning: Truthfulness and honesty run through every list of virtues; the Kena says truth is the very home of the highest teaching.
applies_when: Someone is tempted to lie, cover up, or present a false image.
misleads_when: It is used to justify brutal honesty that does needless harm, or to demand disclosure that would put someone in danger.
modern_application: Identify one area where you are not being fully honest, and take one step towards truth there.

name: Don't unsettle others; meet them where they are
meaning: The wise should not unsettle those attached to their way of acting, but encourage them by example; God receives people however they approach.
applies_when: Someone wants to change a family member's or friend's beliefs or habits, or impose their own new insight.
misleads_when: It is used to stay silent about something harmful.
modern_application: Instead of arguing, live the change yourself for a month and let others ask you about it.

name: Respect the different ways people seek
meaning: Whatever form people worship with faith, God makes that faith steady; even those devoted to other gods are, in their way, seeking the same.
applies_when: Interfaith or intergenerational tension about religious practice in a family or friendship.
misleads_when: It is used to claim all practices are equally wise, or to excuse harmful practices.
modern_application: Ask the other person what their practice means to them, and listen without correcting.

name: Love without clinging
meaning: Among the marks of knowledge is not clinging to son, spouse and home, with evenness amid the welcome and the unwelcome. Śaṅkara stresses detachment; Rāmānuja reads it as not clinging beyond their role in one's duties.
applies_when: A parent struggles to let an adult child make their own choices, or someone's peace depends entirely on others' approval.
misleads_when: It is used to justify emotional neglect, or to urge someone to leave their family. Restricted for under-18s and anyone in distress.
modern_application: Ask: am I trying to care for this person, or to control the outcome of their life? Keep the care and loosen the control.

name: Nourish one another
meaning: 'Nourishing one another, you will reach the highest good': mutual care is the basic pattern of a good life.
applies_when: A relationship or team has become one-sided or transactional.
misleads_when: It obliges someone to keep nourishing a relationship that only harms them.
modern_application: Ask the other person what would help them this week, and tell them one thing that would help you.

name: The wise see the same in all
meaning: The wise see the same in a learned person, an animal and an outcaste; those established in sameness have overcome the world here and now.
applies_when: Prejudice by caste, class, religion, gender or status is affecting how someone treats others or is treated.
misleads_when: It is used to deny that real injustice exists ('we are all the same, so there is no problem').
modern_application: Notice whom you instinctively treat with more or less respect, and correct it once this week.
